transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you for seeing me. I, um, I hope I'm doing this right. It's probably nothing too serious, just a little... well, a little embarrassing to admit, I guess. My wife actually pushed me to make the appointment. 

What really brought me in is that, well, she’ll be telling me about my cousin’s appointments or, you know, figuring out his rides and things. And I’m looking right at her, nodding along... but a minute later I realize I didn’t actually take in half of what she just said. 

I mean, I'm sure everyone gets a little distracted sometimes, right? It's not like I'm doing it on purpose. But it happens enough that she's getting pretty frustrated with me. Is that... does that make sense for why I'd be here?
Have you had this kind of trouble paying attention for most of your life, even back when you were a child or teenager?

Well, um, I suppose so, yes. I mean, I hope it's okay to say this, but I was never a troublemaker or anything! My teachers actually told my parents I was quite bright, which was always nice to hear. 

But, um... yeah, back in grade school, probably before I was 12 or so, they did say I was always daydreaming. I guess I'd just get a little lost in my thoughts. And I'd sort of... accidentally leave my homework inside my desk, or the teacher would have to remind me to finish up my classwork. I always thought that was just normal kid stuff, you know? Just having your head in the clouds a bit. I wasn't doing it to be difficult. 

Is that... does that answer your question? I hope I'm giving you the right information.
Besides at home with your wife, does this trouble paying attention also cause problems for you at work?

Well, um, I'm actually retired now, so I don't have a traditional job anymore. But I do help out with a little catering business on the side, just to stay busy, you know? It's nothing major. 

I guess... well, I do sometimes have to double-check things or redo small tasks, just to make sure I don't mix up the orders. I really try my best to stay on top of it, I promise. I just want to make sure I do a good job for them. 

And, um, at home... well, like I mentioned, my wife is getting a little frustrated. It's causing some tension because she feels like she can't completely count on me when it comes to helping with my cousin's care. I feel terrible about it, really. I want to be helpful, I just... things slip my mind. 

I hope that's not too terrible to admit. Does that sound like the kind of thing you were asking about?
Have you noticed that your attention or memory has gotten worse in the past few years?

Well, um... I wouldn't say my memory is going bad or anything! I hope not, anyway. I'm still doing pretty okay for my age. But, to be completely honest, it has been noticeably harder to keep track of things for about... oh, maybe the last 11 months or so? 

That was when my cousin moved in with us, right after his surgery. There's just a bit more going on in the house now, and I think maybe I just get a little overwhelmed trying to juggle the extra routine. I really do try my best to stay focused on it all, I promise. It's just a lot of new information at once. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
When you’re having trouble taking things in, do you usually feel worried or on edge at the same time?

Well, um... no, I wouldn't say I feel worried or on edge. I'm actually a pretty relaxed guy, mostly! I hope that's a good thing. 

It's not really a nervous feeling at all. It's more just... well, my mind just sort of drifts off quietly, I suppose. I usually don't even realize I'm not taking things in until after the fact, so I'm not sitting there feeling anxious while it's happening. I try to keep a positive attitude about it all, you know? I really don't want you to think I'm a nervous wreck or anything like that. 

Is that... does that make sense for what you're looking for? I hope I'm answering that right.
Have you started having trouble managing things like bills, medications, or appointments on your own?

Well, um... I wouldn't say I'm having *trouble* managing those things, exactly. I mean, I'm still handling everything, for the most part! I don't want you to think I'm completely falling apart or anything. 

But, I suppose... well, lately, there have been a few little slip-ups. Just minor things, really. Like, I meant to return a call from the doctor's office the other day and it just completely slipped my mind. And, um, there was a time I forgot to pick up a prescription while I was out. Oh, and I guess we've been cutting it a bit close leaving the house on time for a couple of my cousin's appointments. 

I feel awful about it, I really do. I try to stay organized, I promise. It's just... I guess I've been a little forgetful with some of those day-to-day things. I hope that doesn't sound too irresponsible of me. Is that the sort of thing you meant?
Do other people besides your wife think your memory has been getting worse?

Well, um... no, I don't think anyone else has really said anything about it. I mean, my cousin hasn't mentioned it, and we spend a lot of time together now. 

I try really hard to keep things running smoothly so nobody else has to worry, you know? I'd hate to be a burden on anyone. So, if anyone else has noticed, they haven't brought it up to me. I think I do a pretty good job of keeping it together when I'm around other people, for the most part. 

I really hope that means it's not as bad as it feels sometimes. Does that sound okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Has your wife told you that she thinks your memory or attention has gotten worse lately?

Well, um... she might have mentioned something once or twice, but I really don't think it's anything major. You know how spouses can be, right? They just worry because they care. 

She might have said something about me seeming a little distracted sometimes, or maybe forgetting a little detail here and there, but I promise I'm really trying my best to stay on top of things. I don't want her to have to worry about me, and I certainly don't want you to think I'm just ignoring her or anything like that. I listen to her, I really do. 

I think she just notices the little things more because we're always together. But it's not like she's sitting me down for a serious talk about it or anything. I hope that makes sense? I just want to be sure I'm not making it sound worse than it really is.
Have the people who know you best noticed a clear change in your thinking compared with how you used to be?

Well, um... no, I really don't think so. I mean, nobody has ever come up to me and said, "Hey, you're not as sharp as you used to be," or anything like that! 

I try to stay on top of things, I really do. I think I'm still just as capable as I've always been, for the most part. Like I said, maybe a little distracted here and there, but nothing that would make my family or friends think I've really changed. I wouldn't want them worrying about my mind going or anything like that. 

I hope that's a good sign? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture. I'm really trying to be helpful.
Do you find yourself asking the same question again because you forgot that someone already answered it?

Oh, no, I don't believe I do that. I mean, I really try my best to pay close attention when people are taking the time to talk to me. It would feel awfully rude to make someone repeat themselves just because I wasn't keeping track, you know? I'd feel terrible being a bother like that. 

So, no, I don't think I ask the same questions over again. I might ask for clarification if I just didn't hear them right the first time, but not because I completely forgot they already answered. I try to be very considerate about that sort of thing. 

I hope that answers your question okay? I'm really trying to give you exactly what you need here.
Do you often misplace everyday things like your keys, wallet, or glasses?

Well, um... I suppose occasionally I might misplace something, but I really try to be careful with my things. I mean, doesn't everybody do that now and then? 

I might put down my keys, or my phone... or maybe some catering receipts or my garden clippers, just somewhere in the house. And then I'll have to spend, oh, maybe ten minutes retracing my steps to find them. But I always do find them! I make absolutely sure of it. I'd hate for you to think I'm just losing things left and right or being irresponsible. It's really just a little slip of the mind here and there, and then I get right back on track. 

I hope that's an okay answer? I just want to be honest with you, but I also want to make sure I'm not making it sound like a bigger deal than it actually is.
Do you often have trouble organizing tasks or keeping things in order?

Well, um... I wouldn't say I have *trouble* with it, really. I mean, I like things to be somewhat tidy, you know? 

I suppose my system might not look perfectly organized to someone else, but... but I usually know where things are, eventually. If I'm doing some gardening or looking through old papers, things might get a little spread out on the table for a bit. But I always intend to put them away! I really do try to keep on top of it all. I wouldn't want anyone to think I'm living in a mess or that I can't handle my own affairs. 

Sometimes a project might just... take a little longer to finish up than I planned, so the pieces stay out. But that's just normal, isn't it? I hope that makes sense. I'm just trying to give you the right idea without making it sound worse than it is. Am I explaining that alright for you?
Do you often find that when you read, your mind drifts and you have to go back over the same page because you didn’t take it in?

Well, oh... reading. I suppose, um... well, I do try very hard to focus, especially when it's something important. 

Like, if I sit down to work out a catering order, or maybe I'm listening in on a parish planning call and looking over the materials... I always start off just fine! I'm right there with it. But then, I don't know, sometimes my mind just sort of... takes a little stroll, I guess? And then I'll realize I've been looking at the same page and I have to go back over the notes again, almost like I hadn't just read them. 

But I always catch myself! And I always go back and make sure I get it right. I wouldn't want to mess up an order or miss something for the church, that would be awful. It's just a little fatigue, I'm sure. I mean, at my age, reading those small print notes can just make your eyes tired, right? 

I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you good information without making it sound like I can't pay attention to things that matter.
Outside of home, do you also often drift off or miss what people are saying in conversations with friends, at church, or during your catering work?

Well, um... no, I wouldn't say that happens often. I mean, I try to be very present when I'm talking with people. 

If I'm at church or working with a client on a menu, I'm definitely listening! I suppose... maybe if it's a very long conversation, or if there's a lot of background noise, my mind might wander just a tiny bit for a second, but I always snap right back. I don't think people even notice, and I certainly don't miss the important parts. I wouldn't want anyone to think I was being rude or ignoring them, you know? That would be terrible. 

I really do make an effort to be a good listener. Does that sound normal to you? I hope I'm not giving the impression that I'm just zoning out when people are talking to me.
Has your wife noticed a clear change in your attention or memory compared with how you were a year or two ago?

Well, um... my wife, she... she is wonderful, but she does worry a bit sometimes. I wouldn't say there's been a *clear* change, like something is terribly wrong, you know? 

I suppose... well, things have been just a tiny bit more challenging lately. For about, oh, maybe eleven months now? But there's a very good reason for it! My cousin had surgery and moved in with us around then, so the house has just been a little more bustling than usual. It's just a lot more to juggle, making sure he's comfortable and all. 

So if she's noticed anything, it's just because my plate is a little fuller right now. Anyone would be a bit more scattered trying to manage all that, don't you think? I just wouldn't want you—or her—to think my mind is going or anything like that. It's just a temporary adjustment, really. Am I making sense? I hope that explains it alright.
Do you often start tasks but leave them unfinished because you lose focus partway through?

Well, oh... leaving things unfinished. I try very hard not to do that, I really do. I always intend to finish everything I start. 

I suppose, um... well, occasionally, I might start something simple, like, oh, setting up my cousin's pill organizer for the week, or maybe wiping down the prep tables after I've been doing some cooking. And I'll get right to it! But then, maybe the phone rings or I think of something else I need to grab from the other room, and... well, I might notice a bit later that I left one or two little steps unfinished. 

But I always go back and finish it as soon as I realize! It's never anything major, just a tiny oversight here and there. I mean, with everything going on, it's easy to get pulled in a few directions at once, isn't it? I certainly don't just abandon things on purpose. I hope that doesn't make me sound irresponsible or careless... I really do try to stay on top of it all. Does that seem like a normal thing to happen when you're busy?
When you’re by yourself doing routine things, do you also lose track of what you were doing?

Oh, um... by myself? No, no, I wouldn't say that happens. When I'm just going about my normal day, doing my regular chores around the house, I stay right on track. 

I mean... I suppose everyone walks into a room and forgets what they went in there for once in a great while, right? But I certainly don't just lose track of what I'm doing in the middle of a routine. I have my little daily habits, and I stick to them very well. 

I wouldn't want you to worry that I can't manage on my own or that I'm just wandering aimlessly around the house. I take a lot of pride in keeping things running smoothly, especially with my cousin living here now. I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for? I just really want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how things are.
When your wife is talking to you, does this happen with almost any topic, or mainly when she’s explaining your cousin’s care?

Well, um... I suppose it's mostly... mostly when it's about my cousin's care. That's really the main thing, to be honest. It's actually sort of what brought me in to see you today. 

My wife, she's so wonderful and organized, and she'll be telling me about his upcoming appointments, or who is giving him a ride on what day, and... well, I'm looking right at her, nodding along, trying to be a good listener. But then, maybe a minute later, I realize I didn't actually take in half of what she just said. 

I feel just terrible about it when it happens! I don't want her to think I don't care, because I do, very much. It's just... well, it's a lot of details to keep straight all of a sudden, you know? With the schedules and the times. I'm sure anyone would get a little overwhelmed by all those logistics, right? I really hope that doesn't make me sound like a bad husband. I do try my very best to pay attention. Is that... is that the sort of thing you were asking about?
Before your cousin moved in, were you having this same problem when your wife talked to you?

Oh, no, no, not really. Before he moved in, things were quite manageable, they really were. We've always had wonderful conversations, my wife and I. 

It's just... well, it's really just been the last 11 months or so that it's gotten noticeably harder. Ever since my cousin had his surgery and came to stay with us. It's just been such a big change to our routine, you know? So many new things to keep track of all at once. 

Before that, I was always very attentive. I still am, mostly! It's just this one particular area that's been a little tricky lately. I'm sure it's just the stress of the adjustment, don't you think? I mean, anyone would struggle a little bit with such a sudden change in the household, right? I just want to be sure I'm explaining it clearly so you don't think I've always been this way.
